<reason>Both sides were disciplined and adapted well, but B controlled the decisive clashes. On efficacy, B anchored "meaningful reduction" to the only observed statewide test (Arizona displacement into same-county cash work) and exposed A's retreat to an unquantified "material decline" as unfalsifiable; A's national-coverage point was neutralized by the argument that the escape valve is off-payroll, not geographic. On discrimination, B's mechanism (mismatch costs attach only to foreign-seeming applicants, converting latent bias into a prescreening filter) plus the invisible-victim problem survived A's paired-testing answer, which B convincingly reframed as counting victims after harm rather than preventing it. On shortages, A landed a real hit (H-2A has no statutory cap), but B recovered with "uncapped on paper, capped in fact," and the seasonal compression point stood. A's closing asymmetry attack was sharp, but B answered it head-on with the downhill/uphill framing. B used hedged, plausible empirical anchors without fake precision and won the weighing in nearly every round.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2: converting A's H-2A answer into "those constraints are the labor shortage, renamed" and A's paired-testing safeguard into the concession that victims "can only be counted" — turning both of A's direct answers into evidence against the motion.</best_rebuttal>
